clue.text: Hidden half of proverb

definitions.meaning: the first half of the saying that ends 'out of mind'

explanation.definitionFit: Something concealed cannot be seen, and the phrase is also the opening half of the proverb about absence and forgetting.

clue.text: Contents of some bar that is found in' US city

annotationWithheld.why: Contents of some bar that is found in US city (5): OM (middle of 'some') + AHA ('that is found!') fits OMAHA, but 'bar' then has no job; no parse found that uses every word
annotationWithheld.clue: Contents of some bar that is found in' US city

clue.text: Classified with respect to variety

indicators.note: variety implies a different arrangement, so the letters of the two words before it are mixed up

explanation.surface: Something is sorted into classes according to its variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' signals an anagram of RESPECT TO; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified documents are restricted, kept hidden from the public by government rule.

clue.text: Not allowed date, say, with object of desire?

parts.note: something not allowed is forbidden
a date is an example of a fruit, the 'say' marking the example

explanation.surface: A banned date, perhaps a romantic one, involving someone the speaker longs for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' looks like a romantic outing but is the palm fruit; the question mark marks the definition as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempting thing that is all the more wanted because it is prohibited, after the apple in Eden.

clue.text: State of mind I analyse in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A psychologist describes a state of mind that they partly analyse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of mind' looks like one phrase, but 'State' alone is the definition, a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Midwest, capital Indianapolis.

clue.text: Behan character's call for attention on the boards

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: ho is an old shout to attract attention
the boards is a theatrical idiom for the stage

explanation.surface: A figure in a Brendan Behan play shouts for attention while performing in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Brendan Behan was an Irish playwright whose play 'The Hostage' gives the title figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The title role of Brendan Behan's play is a captive held by the IRA.

clue.text: Kind behaviour

explanation.definitionFit: A sort or variety; also manners or conduct by accepted standards, as in 'good form'.

clue.text: Bulb I planted in mounting numbers

indicators.note: planted in means the letter is put inside the other piece, like a seed in soil
mounting in a down clue means the word is read going upwards, so backwards

parts.note: NO is an abbreviation for number, so numbers gives two of them

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a bulb among a growing number of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns NONO into ONON, and 'planted in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable grown as a swollen underground bulb, used in cooking.

clue.text: Expert with solution that opens many doors

definitions.note: the relative clause stands for a thing which opens many doors

parts.note: a master is an expert
a key is the solution to a puzzle

explanation.surface: A specialist with an answer that gives access to many opportunities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opens many doors' reads as a figure of speech for opportunity, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A single key cut to work every lock in a building.

clue.text: Constant ' control sometimes used in drawing

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun: a thing sometimes used to draw a game

parts.note: perpetual means constant, never ceasing
to check is to control or restrain

explanation.surface: An artist keeps tight control over their sketching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests art, but it is drawing a chess game, where endless checks force a draw.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a player who can give check forever forces the game to be a draw.

clue.text: Was high-minded, like sanctimonious inner circle

parts.note: as means like
pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious
on a dartboard the inner bull is the red circle at the centre

explanation.surface: Someone was principled, like a smug clique of insiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inner circle' suggests a clique, but it is the red ring of a target.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's sights on lofty goals, an ambition of the mind.

clue.text: Kind that is wearing glasses

indicators.note: the glasses are worn around the other piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: A sort of person who wears spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: A biological category, a sort or type of living thing.

clue.text: Letters from maniac are in US collection

indicators.note: the letters of maniac and are are taken and rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Letters written by a madman form part of an American archive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Things typical of American history and culture gathered together.

clue.text: Write to church, for change

parts.note: to pen is to write
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone writes to their church asking for a change of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' means loose coins here, not alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: Small coins in British money are loose cash carried in a pocket.

clue.text: Fragment to drop right in the ." middle

indicators.note: the letter for right goes in the middle of the other word

parts.note: to shed is to drop, as leaves are shed

explanation.surface: Instruction to drop a piece right in the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap or small torn piece of something.

clue.text: Newspaperman, one taking action without foundation

indicators.note: without means outside, so the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a suitor in old legal use is one bringing a lawsuit, taking legal action
a bed is a foundation layer, as a bed of concrete

explanation.surface: A journalist acts with no basis for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who checks and corrects copy before publication.

clue.text: Cowed a multitude without point

indicators.note: without means outside, so a ruck goes around the point

parts.note: a ruck is a crowd or throng
west is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A crowd lacking any purpose was intimidated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without point' reads as 'pointless' but means a compass point placed inside A RUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled with reverential fear or wonder, overawed.

clue.text: It is customary to turn in wet when at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the three words before are thrown about

explanation.surface: Sailors traditionally turn in when the weather gets wet at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule kept by tradition rather than written down, like an unwritten law.

clue.text: Like Flora's odd action in French dance

indicators.note: in means the scrambled letters go inside the dance

parts.note: bal is French for a ball or dance

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of action are scrambled

explanation.surface: Flora does something strange at a French dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' scrambles the six letters of 'action' before 'in' puts them inside. 'Flora' looks like a woman's name but means plant life.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to plants, which is what flora means collectively.

clue.text: Wine essential to BBC, roughly speaking

indicators.note: roughly speaking says the words sound approximately like the answer

parts.note: essential is key, and Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: A wine is said to be vital to the British broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC, Britain's public broadcaster, is fondly called 'Auntie'.
explanation.definitionFit: A red from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Dropped right in this? No, no!.

definitions.text: Dropped right in this? No, no!

parts.words: Dropped right in this? No, no!
parts.note: replace each word of 'right in' with its opposite to get the phrase for dropped

explanation.definitionFit: To be excluded or omitted from a team or list.

clue.text: Invariably archaic

parts.note: the clue asks for an old-fashioned word meaning at all times

explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic form, without its final S, meaning at all times.

clue.text: Steep around Beachy Head — keep out

indicators.note: the expensive word goes around the letter

parts.note: steep means expensive, dear

indicators.note: head means the first letter of Beachy

explanation.surface: A steep slope around the Sussex cliff Beachy Head, marked as off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: Beachy Head is a chalk headland on England's south coast; here 'Head' just takes B.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar or exclude someone from a place or right.

clue.text: Summary champion holds for somebody

definitions.meaning: a champion here is an advocate, who holds a case for a client

explanation.definitionFit: A short concise account; also the set of instructions a barrister is given to argue a client's case.

clue.text: Bending with 19, a cause of ill-feeling

indicators.note: the answer to 19 says the letter for left is to be removed

parts.note: inflection is a bending or curving

explanation.surface: Bending over while left out, someone feels unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 down is 'left out', so L (left) is taken out of the bending word.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease caused by germs makes a person feel unwell.

clue.text: Biting cold

explanation.definitionFit: Inclined to nip like a snappy dog; also describes chilly, sharp weather.

clue.text: Training unit to manoeuvre without one

indicators.note: without means outside, so the scrambled letters go around the numeral
manoeuvre means move about, so the letters of unit and to are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A military unit is training to manoeuvre without a single soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' makes TUITON from the six letters before it; 'one' is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching or instruction, especially paid lessons.

clue.text: Excel in public works

parts.note: overt means open, public
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone shines in civic engineering projects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'public works' looks like one phrase but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise above or surpass others.

clue.text: Flier able to defeat even ace

definitions.meaning: in bridge, a trump card played on a suit beats even its ace

explanation.definitionFit: A wading bird; also, in card games, trumping, which can beat even an ace.

clue.text: In my case, one's deceived and left in error

indicators.note: my forms a case around the other pieces

parts.note: one's is I's, the Roman numeral I plus S
taken in, so taken means deceived

explanation.surface: Someone admits they were fooled and wrongly abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In my case' reads as a personal aside, but 'case' signals a container; 'taken' as in 'taken in' means fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongly, by a misjudgment.
